name: Minutes a room is in use
brief:
A meeting room's log lists bookings as `[start, end]` minute pairs, meaning the room is booked from `start` up to but not including `end`. Bookings can overlap and come in any order. Return the number of minutes in which the room has at least one booking.

Write `booked_minutes(bookings)`.

Example. For `[[30, 60], [0, 45], [90, 100]]` the first two together cover minutes 0 to 60, and the third adds 10, so the answer is 70.
constraints: $O(n \log n)$ time is the target. Marking each booked minute one by one is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Sort by start and keep the current merged stretch. When the next booking starts after the stretch ends, add the stretch's length and begin a new one.

examples.note: Minutes 0 to 60 count once, and 90 to 100 add 10.
The bookings touch at minute 5 without overlapping, so the total is 5 plus 3.
An empty log books no minutes.

tests.call: booked_minutes([[j * 1000, j * 1000 + 1500] for j in ((i * 7919) % 200000 for i in range(200000))])
booked_minutes([[j * 10, j * 10 + 3] for j in ((i * 7919) % 200000 for i in range(200000))])

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: After sorting by start, overlapping bookings sit next to each other, so one pass merges them into stretches.
Adding every booking's length is the trap: minutes inside an overlap are then counted twice.
The sort costs $O(n \log n)$ and the pass $O(n)$, with $O(n)$ space for the sorted copy.
